guion_largo.texto:
A ramp is a sloping path, without steps. This one has something special: it is made of slabs with engraved animals.

According to the INAH guide, it has two hundred seventy slabs. México Desconocido counts two hundred fifty-five. Medina Romero speaks of two hundred seventy-one, within a total of more than four hundred engraved slabs found at the site. The figures do not agree. That is why here we say: more than two hundred fifty.

Medina Romero adds that many of the engraved species still exist. That is, those who carved them looked at their surroundings and drew them in stone. Kenneth Hirth speaks, instead, of mythical animals. Both descriptions can be true at once: a ramp with real fauna and imagined fauna.

INAH Lugares explains that the ramp connects with the east ball court. That suggests that the game and the ramp were part of the same complex.

The animal remains from the city tell something similar. According to Eduardo Corona, jaguar, peccary, bobcat and river crocodile appear mostly in the high areas, almost always turned into ornaments or offerings. Deer, dog and puma appear on all levels. In the lower part there are catfish, ducks, turtles and otters.

Look for an animal you know and another that does not ring a bell. Think that someone chose which animals to put and in what order.

texto.Engraved slabs: two hundred seventy (INAH), two hundred fifty-five (México Desconocido), two hundred seventy-one of more than four hundred (Medina Romero)

texto.pregunta: Myth: All the animals on the ramp are mythical.
texto.respuesta: Reality: Medina Romero indicates that many of the engraved species still exist. Hirth, on the other hand, speaks of mythical animals.
